name: Gaius
overview: Gaius is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament as a traveling companion of the Apostle Paul from Macedonia. Beyond this role, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or personal background. His primary identification is connected to his association with Paul's missionary journeys.
namesAndTitles: The name Gaius appears as a proper name in the New Testament without a specific meaning or divine origin noted. There is only one recorded instance of this name associated with him, found in Acts 19:29.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Gaius beyond his connection to Paul as a traveling companion. No other relational details are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Gaius is significant in the biblical narrative as a faithful companion who accompanied Paul during his ministry in Macedonia. His presence alongside Paul highlights the support network that enabled the spread of the Gospel during the early church era. Although brief, his mention underscores the collaborative nature of apostolic missions.
